items.title: Market Outlook: Which Canadian Stocks Could Outperform Before Year-End? - The Globe and Mail
items.body: Market Outlook: Which Canadian Stocks Could Outperform Before Year-End? Canadian Stock Market Outlook (About StockTargetAdvisor.com (STA Research) is a Canadian investment research company specializing in advanced stock research and analysis). Canadian stocks are entering the final weeks of 2026 with investors facing a difficult question, will the market recover from its recent volatility, or will higher interest rates and economic uncertainty lead to further declines? The outlook remains cautiously positive, but not all sectors are likely to perform equally. Companies with strong earnings, stable cash flow and attractive valuations may outperform, while highly valued technology stocks and businesses sensitive to borrowing costs could experience greater volatility. The S&P/TSX Composite Index closed November 24th at approximately 33,962 points, following a sharp rebound earlier in the week. The recent movements show that investor confidence remains fragile, particularly in technology and mining stocks. One of the biggest concerns heading into December is the Bank of Canada’s interest-rate policy. The central bank increased its overnight rate to 2.50% in October as inflation remained elevated. With inflation running at 3.1% in October and economic growth expected to remain relatively modest, another interest-rate increase remains a possibility before year-end. Higher borrowing costs can reduce consumer spending, slow housing activity and pressure business investment. They can also make bonds and other income-producing investments more attractive relative to stocks. However, companies with healthy balance sheets, pricing power and dependable earnings may continue to perform well even in a challenging economic environment. Canadian Stocks That Could Outperform Before Year-End 1. Royal Bank of Canada (RY:CA) — Financial Stability and Earnings Strength Royal Bank remains one of Canada’s leading financial institutions, supported by its diversified banking operations, wealth management and capital markets businesses. Its strong profitability and established market position provide a degree of resilience during periods of economic uncertainty. Recent analyst revisions have been somewhat cautious, with CIBC lowering its price target from C$300 to C$294 while maintaining Neutral, and National Bank reducing its target from C$321 to C$314 while maintaining Outperform. Despite the reductions, RBC remains a potential candidate for investors seeking exposure to a profitable, established Canadian financial institution. The principal risks are slowing loan growth, rising credit losses and the possibility that higher interest rates weaken economic activity. Outlook: Selectively positive for investors seeking financial-sector exposure, although near-term performance may remain sensitive to interest-rate expectations and bank earnings. 2. Enbridge (ENB:CA) — Reliable Cash Flow and Dividend Income Enbridge may offer a more defensive alternative to higher-growth companies. Its extensive energy infrastructure network generates substantial recurring cash flow, supported by regulated operations and long-term commercial arrangements. The company reaffirmed its 2026 financial guidance following its third-quarter results and continues to invest in energy infrastructure projects. This provides investors with exposure to North American energy demand while potentially reducing sensitivity to short-term commodity-price movements. However, Enbridge is not immune to higher interest rates. Its significant capital investment requirements and debt financing costs can influence valuation and dividend growth. Outlook: Constructive for income-oriented investors seeking relatively stable cash flow, although higher bond yields could limit near-term share-price appreciation. 3. Agnico Eagle Mines (AEM:CA) — Gold Exposure and Financial Strength Agnico Eagle remains an important Canadian gold producer with established mining operations and a comparatively strong financial position. Gold can benefit when investors become concerned about economic stability, geopolitical risks or the purchasing power of currencies. Higher gold prices can also improve mining profitability, particularly for producers capable of controlling operating expenses. Agnico Eagle’s net cash position provides flexibility to finance operations and growth projects without depending heavily on external capital markets. Nevertheless, mining shares can experience sharp fluctuations when gold prices decline or production costs increase. Outlook: Positive for investors seeking exposure to precious metals, particularly if financial-market volatility supports renewed demand for gold. 4. Cameco Corporation (CCO:CA) — Long-Term Nuclear Energy Growth Cameco offers exposure to the growing importance of nuclear power within the global energy system. Rising electricity demand, energy security concerns and the expansion of artificial intelligence data centres are supporting interest in reliable, low-carbon electricity generation. The company’s uranium operations, fuel services business and ownership interest in Westinghouse provide several opportunities to benefit from nuclear industry investment. Recent analyst coverage included a TD Securities Buy recommendation with a C$188 price target. However, Cameco’s shares can be volatile because market expectations depend heavily on uranium prices, nuclear investment and future earnings growth. Outlook: Constructive over the longer term, but investors should remain selective about valuations and recognize the possibility of substantial near-term price swings. 5. Celestica (CLS:CA) — AI Infrastructure Growth Celestica remains one of Canada’s most interesting technology companies because of its exposure to advanced computing equipment, networking hardware and data centre infrastructure. items.body: Kestrel Gold Announces Letter of Intent with Eagle Plains for Option of the MPW Project, British Columbia CALGARY, AB / ACCESS Newswire / November 24, 2026 / Kestrel Gold Inc. KGC ("Kestrel") is pleased to announce it has entered into a non-binding letter of intent ("LOI") with Eagle Plains Resources Ltd. EPLEGPLF ("EPL" or "Eagle Plains") dated November 23, 2026, whereby Kestrel and Eagle Plains will negotiate and settle the terms of a definitive option agreement (the "Option Agreement") for Kestrel to acquire up to an 80% interest in Eagle Plains' wholly-owned Mount Polley West (MPW) copper gold project ("the Project"). The 7,407 ha MPW Project is located 54 kms north-northeast of Williams Lake and adjacent to Imperial Metals' Mount Polley Property, in British Columbia's Cariboo region. Management of both Eagle Plains and Kestrel consider MPW to hold excellent potential for copper-gold porphyry and epithermal gold mineralization. The property is owned 100% by Eagle Plains, with a portion of the property subject to Net Smelter Royalties held by third parties, including Summit Royalties. LOI Terms Under the terms of the LOI, on order to exercise the Option, Kestrel must make a series of cash payments and share issuances to Eagle Plains and fund exploration expenditures on the Project. These payments, share issuance and expenditures are separated into two phases, with the First Option entitling Kestrel to acquire a 60% interest in the Project by paying CA$350,000, issuing an aggregate of 2,400,000 common shares to EPL and funding CA$5,000,000 in exploration expenditures on the Project by over a four-year term. Pursuant to the Second Option (if elected by Kestrel), Kestrel may acquire an additional 20% interest in the Project (for a 80% total interest) by notifying Eagle Plains of its intent to increase its interest to 80%, and by making an additional payment of $1,000,000, 50% of which may be paid in shares of Kestrel, at Kestrel's election. If either the First Option or the Second Option is exercised, a 2% smelter return royalty will be granted to the Eagle Plains over part of the property, 1% of which may be repurchased for CA$1,000,000. Eagle Plains will serve as Operator under the terms of Option and will reserve the right to use TerraLogic Exploration Inc. as geoscience consultant. Following the exercise of either the First Option or the Second Option, Kestrel and Eagle Plains shall then form a 60/40 or 80/20 joint venture ("JV") to further explore and develop the Property. During the term of the Option, EPL and Kestrel would agree to include any additional claims acquired by staking by either party within a 2km area from existing claim boundaries. A formal agreement with industry standard terms will be prepared, and the expectation is the agreement will be settled and executed by the parties within 30 days. The terms and conditions of the formal agreement will be subject to the laws of the Province of British Columbia, Canada, and subject to regulatory approval. Further details regarding the proposed transaction will be provided in a comprehensive news release if, and when, the parties enter into the formal Option Agreement. There can be no guarantees that the proposed transaction will be completed as contemplated or at all. In addition, 10 documented BC MINFILE mineral occurrences lie within the property boundaries, primarily copper showings. The property is crossed by a paved road, with a network of established logging roads throughout the property. Grid Metals Corp. (TSXV:GRDM) Basic Materials Grid Metals Corp (TSXV:GRDM) 0.17 CAD +0.005 3.030% Last Updated at: 2026-11-24T19:13:00Z is lined up to welcome a deeper strategic investment from Avenir Minerals Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of Agnico Eagle Mines Limited, after Avenir confirmed in a release issued that it expects to increase its interest in the Manitoba explorer. The update is relevant to readers following TSX Penny Stocks, with the TSXserving as the broad Canadian market backdrop. What Avenir's Option Exercise Involves Under the arrangement, Avenir is expected to subscribe directly for common shares of Grid and also to acquire flow-through shares through a charity flow-through structure immediately after closing. Grid stated that no new control person is expected to be created by the placement. Readers following Grid Metals (TSXV:GRDM) Basic Materials Grid Metals Corp (TSXV:GRDM) 0.17 CAD +0.005 3.030% Last Updated at: 2026-11-24T19:13:00Z can track this point in future disclosures. Avenir's own disclosure, issued through CNW Group from Toronto, sets out the steps in more detail. The direct private placement, governed by a subscription agreement would initial lift Avenir's interest to a little. Avenir described the purchase as part of its strategy of acquiring strategic positions in critical minerals opportunities with high geological prospects, and stated that it will file an early warning release under applicable securities laws. Avenir also noted that it has not exercised, and has no present intention of exercising, its right to nominate board members to Grid's board. Avenir describes its mandate as evaluating and advancing critical mineral opportunities, with an initial focus on Canada, and pursuing strategic partnerships and government support. Structure of the Private Placement The financing is a non-brokered private placement. The base offering includes common shares issued to Avenir and Canadian flow-through shares that qualify under the Income Tax Act. The placement also features an upsize option for additional common shares at the same price as Avenir's direct subscription. Grid explained that the upsize exists to accommodate the pre-emptive right of an existing institutional share owner, with that institution deciding whether to participate. The Cesium Resource Behind the Trigger The option became exercisable after Grid published its maiden mineral resource estimate for the Falcon West Cesium Property in southeastern Manitoba, announced so far. The Lucy South deposit contains an open-pit measured mineral resource grading at high levels of both cesium oxide and lithium oxide, as set out in a National Instrument technical release prepared by SGS Canada. Falcon West sits east of Winnipeg along the Trans-Canada Highway, giving the project year-round access to established infrastructure. Grid is the operator of Falcon West, and Avenir already owns a joint venture interest in the property, with the right to increase that interest after a preliminary economic assessment or the adoption of a mine plan. The equity investment in Grid therefore complements Avenir's existing project-level participation. Cesium is a specialized metal with uses in drilling fluids for the oil and gas industry, atomic clocks, specialty glass and advanced electronics, and global production has historically come from a very small number of sources. Where the New Capital Will Be Directed Grid stated that proceeds from the common shares, including any upsize shares, will be used to advance Falcon West toward commercial production and for general corporate purposes. Proceeds from the flow-through shares will fund eligible Canadian exploration expenses that qualify as flow-through critical mineral mining expenditures on Grid's Manitoba portfolio, primarily at Falcon West. Flow-through financing is a common tool for Canadian junior explorers. It allows a company to renounce qualifying exploration deductions to purchasers, and certain critical mineral expenditures attract enhanced federal treatment administered by the CRA. Grid also noted that Manitoba-resident purchasers may be eligible for the provincial Mineral Exploration Tax Credit. Activity of this kind is a regular feature among TSXV penny stocks focused on early-stage discovery and resource development. A Broader Manitoba Portfolio The portfolio includes the Makwa nickel-copper-platinum group metals project, where Teck Resources can earn a majority interest by funding exploration, and the Mayville copper-nickel project on the north arm of the Bird River Greenstone Belt, in which Grid owns the large majority interest. Grid also owns most of the Donner lithium-cesium property adjacent to Mayville, has an option and joint venture with Boliden Mineral Canada on the Thompson East copper-nickel project in north-central Manitoba, and fully owns the Fox River copper-nickel-platinum group metals-gold project in the Gillam region. The company states that its southeastern Manitoba projects are on the ancestral lands of the Sagkeeng First Nation, with whom it has an Exploration Agreement. Market Backdrop for Critical Mineral Juniors Partnerships between senior producers and junior explorers have become a familiar way to fund early-stage critical mineral projects in Canada.
